title: Follow a familiar bedtime routine with your child
subtitle: Brush teeth, read together, then settle for bed
description: Help your child brush their teeth, read together, and go to bed at a regular time.

ageVersions.title: Let your child follow their familiar bedtime routine
ageVersions.subtitle: Brush teeth, read together and settle at the agreed time
ageVersions.description: Let your child follow the bedtime steps you have agreed: brushing their teeth, reading together and settling for bed at a regular time. Stay available if they need support.

title: Switch off bright lights before your child goes to bed
subtitle: Use a dim, warm night-light if needed
description: As bedtime approaches, switch off bright lights in your child’s bedroom. If they need a night-light, use one with dim, warm lighting.

ageVersions.title: Make switching off bright lights part of your child’s bedtime routine
ageVersions.subtitle: Your child can turn off the main light when getting ready for bed
ageVersions.description: Include switching off the bright bedroom light in your child’s bedtime routine. They can do this themselves; if they need a night-light, choose one with dim, warm lighting together.

ageVersions.title: Keep your teen’s bedroom quiet and softly lit before bed
ageVersions.subtitle: Reduce bright light, noise and device distractions
ageVersions.description: Agree with your teen that getting ready for bed includes turning down bright lights and putting devices away. Ask about noise that makes it hard to settle and work together to reduce it.

ageVersions.title: Reduce light and noise that disturb your teen’s sleep
ageVersions.subtitle: Ask what interrupts their sleep and choose a practical change
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen whether light, noise or devices are disturbing their sleep. Discuss a change they can make to their bedroom, then check whether it helps.

title: Put screens away an hour before your child’s bedtime
subtitle: Charge devices outside the bedroom
description: Agree that your child’s screens go away at least an hour before bed. Keep devices outside their bedroom overnight.

ageVersions.title: Make the hour before your child’s bedtime screen-free
ageVersions.subtitle: Keep devices charging outside their bedroom overnight
ageVersions.description: Agree that screens go away an hour before bedtime. Let your child finish using their devices and leave them charging outside the bedroom overnight.

ageVersions.title: Agree on a screen-free hour before your teen’s bedtime
ageVersions.subtitle: Let them set a reminder and charge devices outside their bedroom
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen to set a reminder for an hour before bedtime. When it goes off, they can finish using screens and leave devices charging outside their bedroom overnight.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to finish screen time an hour before bed
ageVersions.subtitle: Let them plan when to stop games, videos and messages
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen to plan their online activities so they can put screens away an hour before bedtime. Keep devices outside the bedroom overnight.

title: Spend time outdoors with your child in the morning
subtitle: Make daylight part of the morning routine
description: Encourage time outdoors in natural light, especially in the morning. Choose a safe activity that suits your child.

title: Help your child keep regular bedtime and wake-up times
subtitle: Keep your child’s sleep schedule similar on weekends
description: Help your child keep bedtimes and wake-up times within 1–2 hours across the week.

ageVersions.title: Keep regular bedtime and wake-up times with your child
ageVersions.subtitle: Keep weekend sleep times close to the weekday routine
ageVersions.description: Choose bedtime and wake-up times together and make them part of your child’s daily routine. Keep weekend times similar to school days.

ageVersions.title: Choose a bedtime with your teen that fits their school mornings
ageVersions.subtitle: Allow enough sleep before they need to get up
ageVersions.description: Start with the time your teen needs to wake for school and choose a bedtime that allows enough sleep. Let them choose a quiet activity to do before bed.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen whether they are getting enough sleep
ageVersions.subtitle: Adjust sleep times when commitments leave them short of rest
ageVersions.description: Ask how rested your teen feels during the day. If school, work or other commitments leave too little time for sleep, discuss changes to their bedtime and wake-up time.

title: Remind your child to use the toilet before bed
subtitle: For children who wet the bed: keep the toilet easy to reach
description: If your child wets the bed, remind them to use the toilet before bedtime. Make sure they can reach the toilet easily during the night.

title: Listen to your teen’s worries before settling for sleep
subtitle: Make time earlier in the day for longer conversations
description: Acknowledge worries that come up at bedtime. If they need a longer discussion, arrange time during the day to talk them through.

title: Include fruit, vegetables and whole grains in family meals
subtitle: Choose different options across the week
description: Offer fruit, vegetables and whole-grain foods across meals, rather than repeatedly relying on the same foods.

ageVersions.title: Let your child choose fruit and vegetables for family meals
ageVersions.subtitle: Add their choices to the shopping list
ageVersions.description: When planning meals, offer a variety of fruit and vegetables and let your child choose some to include. Add their choices to the family shopping list.

ageVersions.title: Invite your teen to help plan balanced family meals
ageVersions.subtitle: Include fruit, vegetables and whole grains on the shopping list
ageVersions.description: Plan upcoming meals together and ask your teen to help write the shopping list. Include fruit, vegetables and whole grains among the foods you choose.

ageVersions.title: Talk with your teen about choosing balanced meals when eating out
ageVersions.subtitle: Discuss options they enjoy from different food groups
ageVersions.description: Ask what your teen likes to eat away from home. Discuss how they can include a variety of food groups in meals from the places they usually visit.

title: Avoid pressuring your child to eat after they feel full
subtitle: Respect their appetite instead of asking them to finish the plate
description: Offer meals and snacks at predictable times. Let your child decide how much to eat, and avoid asking them to finish their plate when they say or show that they are full.

title: Share a relaxed family meal
subtitle: Make room for friendly conversation
description: Eat together when possible and keep mealtime conversation pleasant, without arguments or lectures.

title: Vary the protein foods you serve your child
subtitle: Include options such as beans, eggs, fish or lean meat
description: Include protein foods such as beans, eggs, fish or lean meat as part of varied meals.

title: Offer your child water instead of sugary drinks
subtitle: Make water an everyday option
description: Offer your child water in place of soda and other sugary drinks.

title: Avoid comparing your teen’s body with anyone else’s
subtitle: Talk about caring for bodies without judging their appearance
description: Avoid comparisons about your child’s body or your own. Talk about caring for the body without ranking people by their size or appearance.

title: Offer your toddler a new food alongside familiar foods
subtitle: Start with a small portion and avoid pressure to take a bite
description: Serve a small amount of a new food with familiar foods. Offer it again on another occasion without bargaining over bites.

title: Walk or cycle with your child on short trips
subtitle: Build movement into family travel
description: When practical, walk or cycle together for short journeys instead of taking the car.

title: Give your preschooler time to run, dance and play
subtitle: Offer several chances to move throughout the day
description: Offer varied movement totalling at least 3 hours across the day. At ages 3–4, include at least an hour of more energetic play. Adapt activities to ability and any individual healthcare advice.

title: Plan time for your child to play sports, cycle or dance
subtitle: Choose activities they enjoy and can manage
description: Build activities your child enjoys into the week, aiming for an average of at least 60 minutes of moderate or vigorous activity daily. Adapt activities for disability or health needs using individual advice.

ageVersions.title: Let your child choose active games or sports they enjoy
ageVersions.subtitle: Make room for different activities during the week
ageVersions.description: Offer a choice of active games or sports suited to your child’s abilities. Let them choose what they enjoy and make time for those activities during the week.

ageVersions.title: Plan time with your teen for sports and other physical activity
ageVersions.subtitle: Choose a mix that builds fitness, strength and movement skills
ageVersions.description: Ask which physical activities your teen enjoys and plan when they can do them. Include a variety that develops fitness, movement skills, muscles and bones.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to make time for regular physical activity
ageVersions.subtitle: Fit activities they enjoy around school, work and other plans
ageVersions.description: Let your teen choose enjoyable activities and decide where they fit in the week. Support changes for their abilities, health needs or other commitments.

title: Play throwing-and-catching games with your child
subtitle: Choose throws and catches they can manage
description: Play throwing-and-catching games suited to your child’s age and ability.

title: Let your child choose their own outdoor game
subtitle: Supervise without directing every part of play
description: Offer a safe outdoor space and let your child decide how to play. Stay available and supervise as their age and the setting require.

title: Encourage your child to move after sitting for a long time
subtitle: Break up long seated activities
description: During long periods of sitting, encourage a movement break such as walking or dancing, adapted to your child’s abilities.

title: Help your child brush their teeth morning and night
subtitle: Use fluoride toothpaste and help while they learn
description: Help your child brush their teeth twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste. Use a rice-grain amount under age 3 and a pea-sized amount at ages 3–6. Help young children brush and supervise until they can brush thoroughly.

ageVersions.title: Let your child brush their teeth morning and night
ageVersions.subtitle: Two minutes each time, using fluoride toothpaste
ageVersions.description: Let your child brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste. Check that they are brushing thoroughly and offer support if needed.

title: Help your child wash their hands before eating and after using the toilet
subtitle: Teach your child to use soap, scrub, rinse and dry
description: Help your child wash their hands with soap and water before eating and after using the toilet. Show them how to scrub for at least 20 seconds, then rinse and dry; give hands-on help while they learn.

ageVersions.title: Make handwashing part of your child’s mealtime and toilet routine
ageVersions.subtitle: Before eating and after using the toilet, with soap and water
ageVersions.description: Have your child wash their hands with soap and water before eating and after using the toilet. They should scrub for at least 20 seconds, then rinse and dry; offer support if needed.

title: Apply sunscreen to your child’s exposed skin before going outdoors
subtitle: Use shade and protective clothing too
description: Use broad-spectrum sunscreen, SPF 15 or higher, on exposed skin 15–30 minutes before going outside. Reapply every two hours and after swimming, sweating or towel drying. Use shade, a hat and protective clothing too.

title: Pack water in your child’s school bag
subtitle: Make drinking water available at school
description: Fill a reusable bottle with water and put it with your child’s school things.

title: Encourage your teen to change out of sweaty sports clothes
subtitle: Put the used clothes in the laundry basket
description: After exercise, encourage your teen to change into clean clothes and put sweaty clothing aside for washing.

title: Make a daily shower or bath part of your teen’s routine
subtitle: Talk about body odour and personal care privately
description: Talk with your teen about making time for a daily shower or bath, including washing underarms and feet. Discuss body odour and deodorant kindly and privately if needed.

title: Practise slow breathing with your child while they are calm
subtitle: Breathe in gently and let the breath out slowly
description: In a quiet moment, practise breathing slowly in through the nose and out through the mouth. Start with one breath for younger children.

title: Help your child notice when anger is building
subtitle: Look for signs such as tense muscles or clenched fists
description: Help your child recognise their own warning signs, such as tense muscles, clenched fists or a faster heartbeat.

title: Help your child put their feelings into words when they are upset
subtitle: Connect the emotion to what happened
description: Listen to what happened and help your young child find words for the emotion they are experiencing.

title: Help your child choose what to do when they start feeling angry
subtitle: Practise a response while they are calm
description: Together choose a response, such as walking away to a safe place or talking to a trusted adult. Practise before anger builds.

ageVersions.title: Practise a way to calm down with your child
ageVersions.subtitle: Try stepping away safely or talking to a trusted adult
ageVersions.description: When your child is calm, choose a response they can use when anger builds, such as stepping away to a safe place or talking to a trusted adult. Practise it together.

ageVersions.title: Help your teen choose what to do when anger starts building
ageVersions.subtitle: Connect an early warning sign with a calming action
ageVersions.description: When your teen is calm, ask how they notice anger building. Help them choose an action to try at that point, such as stepping away safely or talking to a trusted adult.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen what helps them calm down when angry
ageVersions.subtitle: Talk about what worked and what they could try next time
ageVersions.description: At a calm moment, ask which responses helped during a recent angry feeling. Discuss what they might try next time and whom they could ask for help if anger remains difficult.

title: Teach your child to ask for a toy instead of hitting
subtitle: Practise the words after they have calmed down
description: When everyone is calm, explain that anger is allowed but hitting hurts. Help your child practise words for asking or taking turns.

title: Stay calmly nearby while your upset child settles
subtitle: Check safety and wait before discussing behaviour
description: Stay close enough to keep your child safe while the strong feeling passes. Offer calm support; discuss what happened after they can listen.

title: Give your child your full attention during time together
subtitle: Put your phone away and join their play or conversation
description: Set aside one-to-one time with distractions switched off. Join your child in play or conversation about something they enjoy.

ageVersions.title: Spend uninterrupted time doing something your child enjoys
ageVersions.subtitle: Let them choose the activity and put your phone away
ageVersions.description: Ask your child what they would like to do together. Join in and put distracting devices away so they have your attention.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen choose how you spend time together
ageVersions.subtitle: Join their interests without turning the time into a quiz
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen what they would enjoy doing with you. Give them your attention and let conversation develop without pressing them with questions.

ageVersions.title: Make time with your teen for an activity you can do together
ageVersions.subtitle: Choose a time that fits both your schedules
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen to suggest something to do together and agree on a time that works for you both. Put distractions away during that time.

title: Listen to your child, then check you understood
subtitle: Let them finish before putting their meaning into your own words
description: Listen without interrupting. Paraphrase what your child said and let them explain if you misunderstood.

title: Ask your child whether they want advice or just someone to listen
subtitle: Let them tell you what kind of support they need
description: Listen first, then ask whether your child wants you to listen or help them work through a solution.

title: Ask your child what they enjoyed or found difficult at school
subtitle: Listen to their experiences with friends and learning
description: Ask about friends, enjoyable experiences and difficulties, then listen to how your child feels about them.

title: Tell your toddler one specific thing to do at a time
subtitle: Get their attention and use a calm voice
description: Give a short direction naming the action, such as putting a toy in its box. Wait for your child to respond before adding another instruction.

title: Warn your child five minutes before playtime ends
subtitle: Explain which activity comes next
description: Before ending play, give a five-minute warning and explain what will happen next.

title: Talk through a difficult decision with your teen
subtitle: Compare the options and what might happen with each
description: Name the problem together, list possible solutions and discuss the advantages and disadvantages. Agree on a workable choice and check later how it went.

ageVersions.title: Talk through solutions to an everyday problem with your child
ageVersions.subtitle: Compare a few options and choose one to try
ageVersions.description: Ask your child to describe the problem, then list possible solutions together. Compare the options and agree on one to try.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen for their ideas before offering a solution
ageVersions.subtitle: Discuss what might happen with each option
ageVersions.description: When your teen brings you a problem, ask what they think could work. Discuss the likely consequences of their ideas and agree how they will try their chosen option.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen choose a solution and learn from the result
ageVersions.subtitle: Talk through the options, then check how their choice worked
ageVersions.description: For an everyday decision, let your teen compare possible solutions and their consequences. After they try one, ask what worked and what they would change.

title: Teach your child to help set the table before meals
subtitle: Start with items they can carry safely
description: Show your child where table items go, then let them help. Choose items and support to suit their abilities.

title: Describe what your toddler is doing as they play
subtitle: Put their actions into simple words
description: While watching your child play, describe their actions, shapes or colours without turning it into a quiz. Follow what interests them.

title: Help your child practise putting on their own clothes
subtitle: Break dressing into manageable steps
description: Offer easy-to-manage clothes and help with the steps your child cannot yet do. Let them practise at their own pace.

title: Help your child wipe up a small spill they made
subtitle: Show them how to use a cloth
description: For a small, safe spill, show your child how to wipe it up and help as needed. An adult handles hot liquids, broken glass and other hazards.

ageVersions.title: Let your child wipe up a small spill they made
ageVersions.subtitle: Use a cloth for small spills; leave hazards to an adult
ageVersions.description: Let your child use a cloth to wipe up a small, safe spill. An adult handles hot liquids, broken glass and other hazards.

title: Practise a greeting with your child before they meet new children
subtitle: Rehearse a greeting together at home
description: If meeting children feels daunting, role-play saying hello and asking about a game before the visit.

title: Teach your child to put dirty clothes in the laundry basket
subtitle: Show them where used clothes belong
description: Put a laundry basket within reach and show your child where to put clothes that need washing. Help younger children.

ageVersions.title: Make putting clothes in the laundry basket your child’s job
ageVersions.subtitle: Keep a laundry basket within easy reach
ageVersions.description: Keep a laundry basket within reach and let your child put clothes that need washing there when they change. Offer support if needed.

title: Help your child put their toys away
subtitle: Show your child where each toy belongs
description: Help your young child put toys away, giving them support as they learn the task.

title: Let your child help measure ingredients while you cook
subtitle: Show them how to fill and level a measuring cup
description: During a suitable cooking activity, help your child fill and level measuring cups and compare quantities.

ageVersions.title: Cook a simple recipe with your child
ageVersions.subtitle: Let them read the steps and measure ingredients
ageVersions.description: Choose a simple recipe and let your child read the steps and measure ingredients. Supervise food preparation and show them how to use equipment safely.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen cook a simple family meal
ageVersions.subtitle: Stay available for unfamiliar steps or equipment
ageVersions.description: Choose a recipe with your teen and agree which steps they can do safely. Let them prepare the meal, with your help for techniques or equipment they have not learned.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen plan and cook a family meal within a budget
ageVersions.subtitle: Give them responsibility for the recipe and shopping list
ageVersions.description: Agree on a budget and let your teen choose a recipe, shop for ingredients and cook the meal. Stay available for equipment or techniques they have not learned.

title: Give your child a clear role in household chores
subtitle: Write down their jobs and when each needs doing
description: Discuss suitable chores with your child and use a list or chart to show who is responsible and when each job needs doing.

ageVersions.title: Let your child choose a household job to take responsibility for
ageVersions.subtitle: Show them the steps and agree when it needs doing
ageVersions.description: Choose a suitable household job together and practise any unfamiliar steps. Write down what your child is responsible for and when it needs doing.

ageVersions.title: Agree on household jobs your teen can do independently
ageVersions.subtitle: Be clear about the timing and what a finished job looks like
ageVersions.description: Discuss which jobs your teen will take responsibility for. Agree when they need doing, explain what completing each job involves and teach unfamiliar steps.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen schedule their household jobs
ageVersions.subtitle: Fit agreed chores around school, work and other commitments
ageVersions.description: Agree which household jobs your teen is responsible for and let them plan when to do them. Ask them to raise timing clashes so you can discuss a workable schedule.

title: Let your child help clear their plate after a meal
subtitle: Use dishes they can carry safely
description: Show your child where used dishes go and help them carry suitable items after eating.

ageVersions.title: Let your child clear their own plate after a meal
ageVersions.subtitle: Choose dishes they can carry safely
ageVersions.description: Let your child take their used plate to the agreed place after eating. Choose items they can carry safely and offer help when needed.

title: Let your child hear you thank someone for helping
subtitle: Name what you appreciated
description: Model gratitude by thanking someone for a specific helpful action while your child is present.

title: Compare prices and features with your teen before choosing a phone plan
subtitle: Discuss which option fits the family’s needs and budget
description: When choosing a phone plan with your teen, compare features and costs together against the family’s needs and budget.

title: Invite your child to describe the pictures while you read together
subtitle: Build on their comments without turning reading into a quiz
description: With a preschooler, invite comments about the pictures, build on their answers and follow their interest. Keep it enjoyable rather than questioning them on every page.

title: Explore your child’s questions together
subtitle: Look closely, find information or try a simple experiment
description: When your child wonders about something, explore the answer together through observation or a simple experiment. You do not need to know the answer beforehand.

title: Let your child draw or paint without copying a sample
subtitle: Provide materials and let them choose what to make
description: For young children, provide blank paper and suitable drawing or craft materials. Let them explore without copying a model or having their work corrected.

title: Make a list of things your child enjoys doing when bored
subtitle: Let them choose from their own ideas during free time
description: Create a list together based on your child’s interests. Use pictures for younger children, and let them refer to it during free time.

title: Meet as a family each week to discuss plans and concerns
subtitle: Give everyone a turn to speak and write down agreements
description: Meet as a family at a regular weekly time, let everyone speak without interruption, and record agreements. Keep reprimands out of the meeting.

title: Invite your child to draw or photograph something in nature
subtitle: Record what caught their attention and revisit it together
description: When a plant, the moon or changing leaves catches your child’s interest, invite them to draw or photograph it. Offer help with recording their observations so you can revisit them together.

title: Check your child’s homework deadlines together
subtitle: Put assignments and due dates in a planner
description: Review upcoming assignments with your child and record due dates. Help them decide when to work on each task.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your child to record homework deadlines in a planner
ageVersions.subtitle: Check the assignments and due dates together
ageVersions.description: Have your child record each assignment and its due date in their planner. Check the entries together so they know what needs doing and when.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to plan their homework for the week
ageVersions.subtitle: Put deadlines and other commitments on one calendar
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen to put assignments and other commitments on a weekly calendar. Review it together and discuss any clashes.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to plan ahead for competing deadlines
ageVersions.subtitle: Spread the work out and flag an unmanageable workload early
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen to look ahead for assignments due close together and plan when to work on each. Discuss adjustments if their schedule leaves too much work for the time available.

title: Set up a quiet homework space for your child
subtitle: Keep your child’s supplies ready and reduce distractions
description: Provide your child with a well-lit workspace and the materials they need. Reduce distractions such as television and phone calls while they work.

ageVersions.title: Let your child get their homework space ready
ageVersions.subtitle: Gather supplies and clear distractions before they start
ageVersions.description: Let your child gather the materials they need and clear distractions before starting homework. Offer support if the space needs changing.

ageVersions.title: Choose a suitable study space with your teen
ageVersions.subtitle: Agree how to reduce interruptions while they work
ageVersions.description: Let your teen suggest a space where they can study. Discuss distractions and agree how you will check in without repeatedly interrupting their work.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen what would make their study space work better
ageVersions.subtitle: Let them choose practical ways to reduce distractions
ageVersions.description: Ask what interrupts your teen’s concentration while studying. Let them suggest changes to their space and support their plan to reduce distractions.

title: Help your child divide a large assignment into smaller parts
subtitle: Plan manageable work sessions with your child
description: Help your child break a big assignment into sections and make a schedule for completing them.

ageVersions.title: Break a big assignment into smaller steps with your child
ageVersions.subtitle: Write a short task list and choose where to start
ageVersions.description: Look through the assignment together and write down the smaller tasks it involves. Let your child choose a starting point and plan manageable work sessions.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen to plan the steps of a large assignment
ageVersions.subtitle: Set a deadline for each stage before they begin
ageVersions.description: Have your teen list the stages of the assignment and decide when to complete each one. Review the plan together before they start.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to plan and track a large assignment
ageVersions.subtitle: Adjust the schedule as the work progresses
ageVersions.description: Let your teen plan the assignment’s stages and deadlines. Check in at agreed points and discuss changes if the remaining work no longer fits their schedule.

title: Let your child see you reading a book for enjoyment
subtitle: Show that reading can be enjoyable outside school
description: Let your child see you reading for yourself, so reading is something adults enjoy as well as a school task.

title: Help your child invite a friend over to play
subtitle: Let them choose whom to invite and coordinate with the other parent
description: Ask your school-age child whom they would like to invite, then coordinate with the other parent. Give the children space to play while remaining available.

title: Play a card or board game to teach your child to take turns
subtitle: Explain each turn and help when waiting is difficult
description: Play a suitable card or board game and explain whose turn comes next. Offer support while your child learns, instead of requiring independent turn-taking immediately.

title: Respect your child’s choice to refuse a hug or kiss
subtitle: Support their right to say no to unwanted touch
description: Explain that they can refuse unwanted touch, even from familiar people. Respect their answer when offering affection.

title: Practise with your child what to do if they are bullied
subtitle: Speak up if safe, move away and tell a trusted adult
description: Discuss what your child can do if bullied: speak firmly if safe, move away when it is not, and seek help from a trusted adult.

title: Help your child make amends if they have bullied someone
subtitle: Choose a response that addresses the harm they caused
description: Only when your child has bullied someone: involve them in an appropriate repair, such as fixing damaged property or writing an apology. Do not force a meeting with the child who was harmed.

title: Teach your child to ask before borrowing someone else’s belongings
subtitle: Help your child wait for permission before taking an item
description: Model asking to use someone else’s things and waiting for their answer. Remind your child of the same rule when needed.

title: Let your teen explain their view before you respond in a disagreement
subtitle: Hear your teen out without insults or interruptions
description: When you disagree, hear your teen’s perspective calmly before explaining yours. Focus on the issue rather than personal criticism.

title: Teach your child to tell a trusted adult about touch or secrets that worry them
subtitle: Make clear that speaking up is allowed
description: Explain that they can tell a trusted adult about anything that worries or upsets them, even if someone asked them to keep it secret.

title: Volunteer together in an activity suitable for your child
subtitle: Choose a community activity that welcomes children
description: Include your child in a suitable community activity, such as helping with a food-bank meal. Choose an opportunity that welcomes children and fits their abilities.

title: Invite your teen’s friends over so you can get to know them
subtitle: Make friends welcome in your home
description: Create opportunities to meet the friends your teen spends time with, including welcoming them into your home.

title: Talk with your teen about respect and control in relationships
subtitle: Discuss pressure, personal choices and the freedom to disagree
description: With your teen, discuss being able to keep friendships, make choices and disagree safely. Explain how controlling behaviour differs from care.

title: Praise a specific effort your child made
subtitle: Say what they did and why you appreciated it
description: Describe a specific effort or helpful action rather than giving a general label about the child.

title: Let your child do their own homework
subtitle: Offer guidance without taking over
description: Be available to explain or suggest an approach, while letting your child do the thinking and complete the work themselves.

ageVersions.title: Let your child try their homework before offering a hint
ageVersions.subtitle: Explain unclear instructions without supplying the answer
ageVersions.description: Give your child time to attempt the work themselves. If they get stuck, clarify the instructions or suggest an approach while leaving the thinking and answers to them.

ageVersions.title: Ask what your teen has tried before helping with homework
ageVersions.subtitle: Focus your guidance on the part they find difficult
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen to show you where they are stuck and explain what they have tried. Offer guidance on that part without completing the work for them.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to ask their teacher about work they find difficult
ageVersions.subtitle: Help them turn the sticking point into a clear question
ageVersions.description: If your teen keeps getting stuck on homework, ask them to identify what they do not understand. Help them prepare a question and encourage them to ask their teacher.

title: Ask your child to show you the apps and games they use
subtitle: Learn what they do there and how they interact with other people
description: Let your child walk you through a platform they use so you understand its features and how they interact with others there.

title: Agree on screen-use limits with your child
subtitle: Choose screen-free times for meals, homework and bedtime
description: Create a family media plan with expectations and limits suited to your child. Agree on screen-free times such as meals, homework and bedtime, and have adults follow the plan too.

ageVersions.title: Agree on screen-free times with your child
ageVersions.subtitle: Include meals, homework and bedtime in the family rules
ageVersions.description: Decide together when screens will be put away, such as during meals, homework and before bed. Explain the family rules and follow them as adults too.

ageVersions.title: Agree on screen-use rules with your teen
ageVersions.subtitle: Make room for their interests while protecting sleep and schoolwork
ageVersions.description: Listen to how your teen likes to use screens, then agree on limits and screen-free times. Include meals, schoolwork and sleep in the plan.

ageVersions.title: Review screen-use rules with your teen
ageVersions.subtitle: Adjust rules that are not helping them balance daily life
ageVersions.description: Ask how the current rules fit your teen’s responsibilities, sleep and relationships. Discuss what is working and agree on changes where needed.

title: Point out advertisements while watching online content with your child
subtitle: Explain when a video or influencer is promoting something
description: When viewing content together, help your child distinguish advertising, edited material and an influencer’s promotional message.

title: Use correct body-part names when talking with your child
subtitle: Answer their questions calmly in words they understand
description: Use correct anatomical terms calmly when discussing the body or answering your child’s questions.

title: Check your child’s plans before they go out
subtitle: Agree who they will be with and when they will check in
description: Agree where your child is going, who they will be with, and when and how they will check in.

title: Check your child’s car seat, booster or seatbelt before every trip
subtitle: Use the restraint that fits their age and size
description: Follow the seat and vehicle instructions. Use a rear-facing seat until its size limit, then a harnessed forward-facing seat, then a booster until the belt fits properly. Keep children under 13 in the back seat.

title: Check your child’s helmet before each bike or scooter ride
subtitle: Make sure it fits and the straps are fastened
description: Use an age-appropriate, certified helmet for cycling or a non-motorised scooter. Check fit, condition and fastening before riding.

title: Set up privacy controls with your child on a new account
subtitle: Check contact settings, reporting tools and purchase permissions
description: When an age-appropriate account is created, use secure privacy settings and discuss who can contact them, reporting tools and purchase permissions. Explain why passwords should not be shared with friends.

title: Teach your child to ask permission before sharing someone’s photo
subtitle: Model asking first and respecting a refusal
description: Before sharing a photo or video, ask the people pictured for permission and show your child how to do the same. Explain that they should not share it if someone says no, and should remove it if that person later asks.

title: Reassure your child they can show you upsetting online messages
subtitle: Listen calmly and help, even if they made a mistake
description: Make clear that your child can seek help for online experiences, even after a mistake. If they disclose something upsetting, listen and help them work out the next step.

title: Talk with your teen about asking for and respecting consent
subtitle: Explain that anyone can say no or change their mind
description: Discuss asking before sexual touching, respecting a refusal and stopping if someone changes their mind or seems unsure. Agreement to one activity does not mean agreement to another.

title: Make a plan your teen can use to leave alcohol or drug situations
subtitle: Agree on a message or code word they can send for help
description: With your teen, practise declining an offer and agree on an exit plan, such as a code word they can text a family member.

title: Answer your child’s puberty questions without teasing
subtitle: Use factual, age-appropriate explanations
description: Listen to the question and answer plainly. If you do not know, say so and find reliable information together. Let your child choose another trusted adult if they prefer.

title: Explain puberty changes before your child experiences them
subtitle: Ask what they already know and correct misunderstandings
description: Discuss changes such as body hair, a changing voice or periods in simple, factual language. Explain that timing varies; ask a healthcare professional about concerns over unusually early or delayed development.

title: Check that your teen has the toiletries they need
subtitle: Keep washing and personal-care products accessible
description: Ask privately whether your teen needs soap, deodorant, skin-care or menstrual products, and make suitable supplies available.

title: Explain periods and help your child pack spare menstrual products
subtitle: Prepare before their first period
description: Talk about periods before they begin, and help your child keep spare menstrual products and underwear somewhere accessible.

title: Explain a rule and its consequence to your child
subtitle: Give them a chance to respond, then follow through calmly
description: State the rule and a manageable consequence. Give your child a chance to change the behaviour and follow through calmly if necessary.

title: Apologise to your child after shouting or treating them unfairly
subtitle: Own your behaviour and explain what you will do differently
description: When you make a parenting mistake, acknowledge it, apologise without shifting blame, and explain how you intend to do better.

title: Tell your child you love them even when they make a mistake
subtitle: Keep affection separate from achievement
description: Let your child know they are loved through words and affection, including when they have made a mistake.

title: Knock and wait before entering your teen’s room
subtitle: Respect everyday privacy
description: Knock before entering and ask before looking through personal belongings. Discuss privacy expectations together.

title: Let your toddler choose between two options you can accept
subtitle: Use simple choices such as which shirt to wear
description: Offer two suitable options and give your toddler time to choose. Use choices for decisions they can make.

title: Agree on household rules with your teen
subtitle: Discuss expectations and consequences together
description: Involve your teenager in setting family rules and the consequences of breaking them.

title: Offer a different activity when your child starts getting frustrated
subtitle: Redirect early, before the situation escalates
description: When you notice restlessness or frustration building, suggest a change of activity. If your child has hurt someone or is already overwhelmed, address safety and help them settle first.

title: Pause before responding when you feel angry with your child
subtitle: Take slow breaths while keeping your child safely supervised
description: When your anger rises, pause and breathe slowly before responding. Keep your child safely supervised during the pause.

title: Follow through on a promise you make to your child
subtitle: Promise only what you can realistically do
description: When you agree to do something with or for your child, follow through. Make commitments you can keep.

title: Make a morning checklist your child can follow
subtitle: Use words or pictures and let them tick off each step
description: List the steps of getting ready together. Let your child mark each step as it is finished, with help as needed.

ageVersions.title: Let your child get ready using their morning checklist
ageVersions.subtitle: Check missed steps together after they have finished
ageVersions.description: Let your child tick off each getting-ready task as they complete it. Once they have finished, check the list together and go over anything missed.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to use their own morning reminders
ageVersions.subtitle: Let them choose a checklist or reminder system
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen to write down the steps they need to complete before leaving. Let them choose reminders that work for them and discuss any steps where they still need support.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen plan how to get ready and leave on time
ageVersions.subtitle: Work backwards from the time they need to leave
ageVersions.description: Agree on the departure time and let your teen work out when to start getting ready. Ask them to raise any part of the routine where they need support.

title: Help your child plan breaks during longer homework sessions
subtitle: Plan work and rest around your child’s homework
description: Help your child schedule breaks when homework needs a longer work session.

ageVersions.title: Plan homework breaks with your child
ageVersions.subtitle: Agree when to pause and when to return to the task
ageVersions.description: Before a longer homework session, choose break points together. Agree when your child will return to the task and remind them if needed.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to plan breaks during longer study sessions
ageVersions.subtitle: Let them plan both the break and the return to work
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen where breaks fit into their study plan and when they intend to restart. Offer support if they find it difficult to return to the task.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen whether their study breaks are helping
ageVersions.subtitle: Review concentration and how easily they return to work
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen to notice when their concentration drops. Discuss whether their breaks help them return to the task, and let them adjust their work-and-rest pattern.

title: Use a visual timer when your child loses track of task time
subtitle: Show how much time is left without repeated verbal reminders
description: For a child who struggles with time management, use a visual timer or countdown clock during a task so they can see how much time remains.

title: Help your child put finished homework in their school bag
subtitle: Have your child pack their work before moving to another activity
description: After your child checks that their homework is complete, have them put it in the appropriate folder and school bag. Help them with this final step as needed.

ageVersions.title: Let your child pack their finished homework
ageVersions.subtitle: Use their checklist, then check the school bag together
ageVersions.description: Let your child put completed work in their folder and school bag. Have them use their checklist before you check the bag together.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to pack their school bag the night before
ageVersions.subtitle: Check tomorrow’s timetable for the materials they need
ageVersions.description: Have your teen check tomorrow’s timetable and pack the materials they need that evening. Let them choose a reminder that helps them remember to do it themselves.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to track which assignments they have handed in
ageVersions.subtitle: Track both online submissions and work taken to school
ageVersions.description: Ask your teen how they keep track of work that needs submitting online or taking to school. If work is being missed, discuss a way they can record and check submissions.

title: Ask how your child feels about an upcoming event
subtitle: Let them name concerns without suggesting fears
description: Ask an open question about the event and listen. Avoid questions that assume something frightening will happen.

title: Talk through what your child could do if a worry comes true
subtitle: Choose a practical response and someone who can help
description: Discuss the specific worry and who or what could help if it happened. Keep the conversation focused on coping rather than guarantees.

ageVersions.title: Talk with your child about what they could do if a worry comes true
ageVersions.subtitle: Choose a practical step and someone they can ask for help
ageVersions.description: Ask your child to name a specific situation they are worried about. Together, identify a step they could take and a trusted person they could ask for help.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen how they could handle a situation they worry about
ageVersions.subtitle: Discuss realistic options instead of promising it will not happen
ageVersions.description: Listen to the specific worry and ask what your teen could do if it happened. Discuss practical responses without promising that everything will go a certain way.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen what would help them handle a specific worry
ageVersions.subtitle: Let them choose practical steps and the support they want
ageVersions.description: Listen to the worry and discuss realistic ways your teen could respond. Let them choose what to try and when they would ask for more support.

title: Help your nervous child join a group game at their own pace
subtitle: Start with watching, then moving closer if ready
description: Let your child observe before joining. Encourage manageable steps towards playing with others and recognise their effort. Slow down if they become overwhelmed.

title: Use the same brief goodbye when leaving your child at nursery or school
subtitle: Explain when you will return
description: Give your child your attention, use a familiar goodbye and explain your return using an event they understand. Follow through on the plan.

title: Help your children resolve a sibling argument
subtitle: Hear each side, then discuss a solution together
description: Hear each child’s view without interruption, help them suggest solutions and agree on a workable plan.

title: Help your children agree on turns before using a shared game or device
subtitle: Agree which child goes first and when turns change
description: Help siblings agree who uses a shared item first and when turns change. Put the plan somewhere they can check.

title: Tell your children what you appreciated when they helped each other
subtitle: Name the helpful action between siblings
description: When siblings cooperate or help each other, describe the action you appreciated so they know what worked.

title: Choose a regular homework time that fits your child
subtitle: Allow for a snack or play beforehand if helpful
description: Agree on a study time that suits your child; some work better after a snack and play, while others prefer later.

title: Teach your child to help fold the clean laundry
subtitle: Show the steps and work together
description: Demonstrate folding suitable items and let your child help with the family laundry. Give support as they learn.

ageVersions.title: Let your child fold and put away their clean clothes
ageVersions.subtitle: Let them finish familiar items and ask about difficult folds
ageVersions.description: Let your child fold their clean clothes and put them in their usual places. Show them any folds they have not learned, then let them finish what they can.

ageVersions.title: Teach your teen to do a load of laundry
ageVersions.subtitle: Show them how to sort clothes and use the machine safely
ageVersions.description: Demonstrate sorting clothes, choosing machine settings and using laundry products safely. Let your teen practise the steps through to putting clean clothes away.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen take responsibility for their laundry
ageVersions.subtitle: Let them plan washing around access to the machine
ageVersions.description: Let your teen decide when to wash and put away their clothes. Agree on use of shared equipment and offer guidance for unfamiliar fabrics.

title: Ask what your child wants discussed at their teacher meeting
subtitle: Take their questions and concerns with you
description: Before a primary-school teacher meeting, ask what your child wants discussed. Take those questions along and ask how you can support learning at home.

title: Help your child make a plan to save for something they want
subtitle: Choose a specific goal and work out how to reach it
description: Help your child choose something they want to save for and make a plan to reach that goal.
